paraphrases.note: institution 较正式；where to study 更适合口语。
prestigious 指声誉高，不等于适合个人。
module 指学位中的具体课程单元。
full cost 应同时考虑学费与生活费。
open day 是大学集中接待申请者的开放日。
fit 强调个人与课程的匹配。
weigh up 表示综合权衡利弊。

sentences.pattern: Whether + university option + is suitable depends largely on + criterion.
sentences.cn: 某个大学选择是否合适，很大程度上取决于某项标准。
sentences.example: Whether a distant university is suitable depends largely on the support a student can access.

sentences.pattern: Rather than choosing + option + solely on the basis of + factor, applicants should + action.
sentences.cn: 申请者不应只根据某因素选择……，而应……。
sentences.example: Rather than choosing a course solely on the basis of prestige, applicants should examine its content.

sentences.pattern: The more accurately + applicants + assess + needs, the less likely they are to + negative result.
sentences.cn: 申请者越准确评估自身需要，就越不容易……。
sentences.example: The more accurately applicants assess their needs, the less likely they are to leave a course early.

I had my heart set on studying in a coastal city.

mistakes.wrong: I want to enter to a good university.
mistakes.correct: I want to get into a good university.
mistakes.why: enter 作“进入”时不接 to；谈录取更自然地用 get into。

mistakes.wrong: The course contains many practical works.
mistakes.correct: The course includes a lot of practical work.
mistakes.why: work 表示学习或工作内容时通常不可数。

mistakes.wrong: I am considering to study abroad.
mistakes.why: consider 后接动名词，不接不定式。

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Course content should outweigh institutional prestige.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: Applicants should judge a degree primarily by what and how they will study.
writingIdeas.argument: A famous university cannot compensate for a programme that does not suit a student’s interests or preferred way of learning. Module descriptions reveal whether a course is theoretical, practical or flexible, while assessment methods show what work will be expected. A student who enjoys laboratory investigation may struggle on a programme dominated by lectures and final examinations. Careful comparison also reduces the risk of changing degrees after considerable expense. Prestige has value, but educational fit should guide the final decision.

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Financial planning is part of a responsible university choice.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: The full cost of study should be considered before an applicant accepts a university place.
writingIdeas.argument: Tuition is only one component of university expense, since housing, transport and materials can vary sharply between locations. Underestimating these costs may force students into excessive paid work and reduce the time available for study. Applicants should compare realistic monthly budgets and investigate grants before committing themselves. Choosing a less expensive city can sometimes provide greater academic freedom than attending a prestigious institution under constant financial pressure. Transparent cost information is therefore essential to fair access.

speaking.question: What would matter most to you when choosing a university?
speaking.answer: The course itself would come first. I would look at the actual modules and how they are assessed, because an impressive name would not help if I disliked the daily work. Location would still matter, especially the cost of housing and the time needed to travel home. I would probably make a shortlist only after comparing all three factors.

speaking.question: Describe a difficult educational choice you made or may need to make.
speaking.answer: A choice I may have to make is whether to study close to home or move to another city. Staying nearby would be cheaper, and I could keep my present support network. The other course, however, offers a specialist module that fits my interests much better. I would speak to current students and calculate a realistic budget before deciding. It is difficult because the academically stronger option also involves more uncertainty and independence. I would also compare the amount of teaching in small groups, because published rankings would not answer that personal question. Moving away could help me become independent, yet loneliness might affect my study at first. Whichever option I choose, I want the decision to rest on daily realities rather than the excitement of a campus visit.

reading.title: Why University Rankings Cannot Make the Decision
paragraphs: University league tables turn a complex institution into a position on a list. For applicants facing hundreds of possible courses, that simplicity is attractive. A high rank appears to promise excellent teaching, respected qualifications and strong employment prospects. Yet the number is an aggregate: it combines indicators chosen for a broad audience, whereas an individual student has a particular subject, budget and preferred learning environment.

The measures themselves deserve attention. Research income may indicate an active academic department, but undergraduates do not necessarily work with its leading researchers. Student-satisfaction surveys capture experience, although responses can be influenced by expectations and by events unrelated to teaching. Graduate salaries favour courses linked to highly paid occupations and universities located in expensive labour markets. None of these indicators is useless; the problem arises when different evidence is treated as a single judgement of quality.

Rankings can also alter institutional behaviour. When a measure becomes influential, universities have an incentive to improve the figure, sometimes without improving the underlying experience to the same extent. Resources may be directed towards visible facilities or selective admission because these affect reputation. By contrast, careful feedback on first-year assignments or support for commuting students is harder to advertise, despite its importance to daily study.

A more reliable selection process begins with questions rather than positions. Applicants can compare compulsory modules, contact hours, assessment types and opportunities for practical experience. They may ask current students how quickly staff respond when difficulties arise. Cost and accessibility should be calculated for the whole degree, not only the first term. A ranking can identify institutions worth investigating, but it cannot decide whether a specific person will flourish there. The final choice requires evidence at the level of the course and the learner.

Applicants should also treat published information as a starting point that needs interpretation. Two courses may report similar contact hours while organising them differently: one uses large lectures and another small laboratories. Visiting, asking precise questions and comparing written answers can expose these differences. The decision improves when a broad indicator leads to closer enquiry instead of replacing it.

questions.prompt: What is the writer’s main criticism of an overall ranking?
questions.explanation: It combines broad indicators that may not match an individual student’s priorities.
options: It is calculated only from student surveys.
It combines broad indicators that may not match an individual student’s priorities.
It is designed mainly for employers.
